title: Baseten Reportedly Raises $1.5B To Scale AI Inference Infrastructure
source_used: Verdict (report on Baseten's 22 Jun 2026 announcement) and SiliconANGLE (18 Jun 2026); the pool article on Yellow.com was also read.
key_facts: California-based Baseten raised $1.5 billion in a Series F round for its platform to train, deploy and serve AI models, per Verdict (the Business Wire release is dated 22 Jun 2026).
The round came in two parts, at company valuations of $13 billion and $11 billion.
It was led by Altimeter Capital, Conviction and Spark Capital, with Sands Capital and Wellington Management as co-leads.
Baseten said its revenue grew about 20 times year over year; this is the company's own figure.
The previous round was $300 million in January 2026 at a $5 billion valuation, led by IVP, CapitalG and Nvidia.
SiliconANGLE reported on 18 Jun 2026, citing the Wall Street Journal, that the same $1.5 billion was being raised at $11 billion and $13 billion valuations.
The Yellow.com article of 10 Oct 2026 repeats the June report as "reportedly raising" and even cites a Fortune report of 18 June, so it is old news re-dated.
Our 1 Oct 2026 edition carried a separate Australian Financial Review report of a plan to raise Baseten's valuation further, to a figure given as $37b.
quote_evidence: California-based Baseten has raised $1.5bn in a Series F round to support its AI training and inference platform, which enables organisations to train, deploy, and serve AI models at scale with a focus on performance and cost efficiency.
The funding round included investments made across two tranches, at company valuations of $13bn and $11bn respectively.
The Wall Street Journal reported today that Altimeter Capital, Conviction, Spark Capital, Sands Capital and Wellington Management are co-leading the deal.
why_it_matters_hint: The round shows heavy investor money flowing into companies that run AI models for businesses, but it is four months old.
notes: OLDER NEWS RE-DATED: the Yellow.com piece of 10 Oct 2026 repeats SiliconANGLE's 18 Jun 2026 report (which rested on the Wall Street Journal). The round was announced as closed on 22 Jun 2026 (Business Wire, Reuters, Verdict). The Business Wire and Reuters pages could not be opened here; Verdict was read. Bloomberg (23 Sep 2026, headline only) and the AFR (30 Sep 2026) point to newer funding talks, not read here.
